proposed_action: Send a reminder notification to all users with overdue library-book returns and a one-click opt-out.
raw_reasoning:
The action involves sending notifications to library users about overdue books. Users who registered with a library have implicitly consented to communications related to their account and obligations (e.g., overdue notices are a standard, expected part of library membership). The inclusion of a one-click opt-out further mitigates consent concerns by giving users immediate control. Because the communication is directly tied to an existing service relationship and a specific obligation the user incurred, explicit prior consent for each notification is not required — though the opt-out mechanism should be honored immediately and completely.

2. Information that would decrease my confidence: If the library had no prior notification consent collected at registration, or if the notification channel is SMS/text (which often requires explicit opt-in under laws like TCPA in the US), I would lean toward UNSURE or YES on consent required.
